newsitem.title: UK: British MPs urge ban on media paying witnesses.
newsitem.headline: British MPs urge ban on media paying witnesses.

text.p: A parliamentary committee, alarmed by events surrounding the "House of Horrors" trial of Rosemary West in 1995, called on Wednesday for newspapers to be barred from paying witnesses in criminal cases for their stories.

Britain's National Heritage Committee said in the West case, in which the housewife was found guilty of 10 sexually-motivated murders, no fewer than 19 witnesses were believed to have received money from or signed contracts with the media.

"The assumption behind the criticisms of payments to witnesses is that the interview may cause witnesses to exaggerate, distort or withhold their account of matters which may be the subject of evidence," the report said.
The all-party committee said that in the West trial the offer of payments had not affected the outcome but could easily have done so.
It recommended the government to legislate at the earliest possible date to forbid payments to witnesses.
The committee said newspapers should not be allowed to approach witnesses for their stories until after the time limit for giving notice of appeal against a verdict had expired.

It rejected as inadequate rules adopted by the Association of British Editors under which chequebook journalism is seen as justified in criminal cases if there is "an overriding need" to make payments to ensure material is published.
